root_motivation: Prod has no distinguishable human signups and the site (mcphost.dev) is the only public surface -- nothing lists mcphost where MCP users actually browse for servers. The public MCP registry (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) accepts a server.json with a remotes entry for hosted servers; its schema and publisher CLI are fetched at build time and pinned in the repo. Fix: the binary emits its own registry entry from the same constants it serves (name, description, version, public endpoint, transport), the artifact is committed and CI-validated against the pinned schema on every push, and the entry points at the bare one-URL endpoint so a reader of the listing is one connection away from a tenant.
user_persona: A visitor who searches the registry for "mcphost", opens the entry, and copies the remote URL into Cursor to get a personal tenant URL on the first call; Operator Joe, who tags a release and expects the registry to show the new version within the hour; CI, which fails a push the moment registry/server.json drifts from what the binary would generate.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the binary, When `mcphost registry-manifest` runs, Then it prints JSON with name, description, version equal to Cargo.toml, a `remotes` entry whose URL is `MCPHOST_PUBLIC_URL` + `/mcp`, and transport `streamable-http`.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/reglist_ac01_manifest_fields_match_cargo_and_endpoint.rs -- spawns the real binary with $MCPHOST_PUBLIC_URL set to a test value and, separately, unset, asserting the printed JSON's description/version against env!("CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION")/env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") and the remote's url/type.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a committed `registry/server.json` equal to the generator's output, When `--check` runs, Then exit 0; after a description change in source, exit non-zero with a diff.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/reglist_ac02_check_detects_drift.rs -- one case runs --check against the real committed registry/server.json (must exit 0); the other points --check --path at a scratch file with a stale description (can't mutate Cargo.toml's own description for one test in a shared suite binary) and asserts exit 1 plus a +/- diff naming both the stale and fresh lines.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the pinned schema, When the test suite validates the committed `server.json`, Then it passes, and an entry missing `remotes` fails.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/reglist_ac03_schema_validates_committed_entry_and_rejects_missing_remotes.rs -- validates registry/server.json against registry/schema.json composed with this host's own required:["remotes"] rule (the raw upstream schema alone leaves remotes optional, since a server may ship packages instead -- see hard_constraints below), then re-validates with remotes stripped and asserts a validation error.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a push to any branch, When the registry workflow runs on the free runner, Then it executes `--check` and schema validation and fails the push on drift.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/reglist_ac04_workflow_checks_manifest_and_schema_on_every_push.rs -- text assertions over .github/workflows/registry.yml: the `on:` trigger has no `branches:` filter, the `check` job runs on `ubuntu-latest` and both `registry-manifest --check` and the reglist_ac03 suite, and `publish` needs `check` and gates on a `refs/tags/v` ref.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tag `v*`, When the workflow runs with the documented secret present, Then it publishes the entry and the registry returns the new version (Live; evidence: registry lookup after the first tag post-deploy).
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: a live, post-tag observation needing the dev.mcphost DNS TXT verification record at mcphost.dev and the MCPHOST_REGISTRY_PRIVATE_KEY repository secret, both Joe's own open questions per the PRD, neither available to this dispatch. AC2-AC4 already prove --check, schema validation, and the workflow's own structure (including the publish job's tag gate and its graceful no-op until the secret exists) end-to-end short of the live network call.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the README, When a reader opens it, Then it contains the registry link and the one-URL quickstart link, both resolving with HTTP 200.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/reglist_ac06_readme_registry_and_quickstart_links_resolve.rs -- the always-on half parses README's own "Find it in the registry" line for its two markdown links and pins them to the published entry in registry/server.json: the first must be an https registry.modelcontextprotocol.io query whose search term carries that entry's server name, its anchor text must be the full published name, and the second must equal the entry's websiteUrl (so a dropped, re-hosted or drifted link fails with no network). The GETs that prove "resolves with HTTP 200" are Live, gated on MCPHOST_LIVE=1 since not every build environment has egress to registry.modelcontextprotocol.io (same convention as tests/mcphost_team_memory_ac08_live_test_skipped_without_env.rs), and carry a negative control in the same run: a non-existent route on the same registry host, through the same client, must come back non-200. The registry's ?search= path is cold-cache slow (~15s measured before first byte, sub-second on repeat), which is why resolve_status allows a 60s per-request timeout and retries transport failures only -- the earlier 15s flat timeout failed on a cold cache with "error sending request for url", indistinguishable from an environment with no egress.

additional.name_is_not_literally_cargo_pkg_name: AC1's own wording ("name, description, version equal to Cargo.toml") could be read as all three fields being exact Cargo.toml literals, but the upstream schema requires `name` to be `<namespace>/<server-name>` (exactly one `/`, pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`) -- Cargo.toml's bare package name "mcphost" would fail that pattern outright. Resolved by pairing Cargo.toml's package name with the dev.mcphost namespace Joe decided (PRD Open Questions, 2026-10-06), so `name` is built FROM Cargo.toml plus the decided namespace, not a second independent literal; `description`/`version` are the direct Cargo.toml fields.
additional.license_field_is_not_in_the_upstream_sch: The PRD's own requirement 2 lists `license` alongside name/description/version/endpoint/transport/repository, but the fetched-and-pinned upstream server.schema.json's Server/ServerDetail definitions have no `license` property at all. Resolved by adding it as a plain top-level field anyway -- neither definition sets `additionalProperties: false`, so an extra `license` key validates cleanly; confirmed by AC3's own passing test against the real pinned schema.
additional.remotes_required_is_a_project_rule_layer: AC3 says an entry missing `remotes` must fail schema validation, but the upstream schema's ServerDetail leaves `remotes` optional (a server can ship `packages` instead) -- a bare pinned-schema check against a remotes-less entry would still pass. tests/reglist_ac03_*.rs composes the pinned schema (its own `definitions` lifted to the composed document's root, since a $ref nested inside a new `allOf` would otherwise resolve against the wrapper's root instead) with this host's own `required: ["remotes"]`, since mcphost never ships `packages` and a remotes-less entry here has no endpoint left to publish.
additional.ac5_is_deferred_not_implemented: AC5's Then ("the registry returns the new version") is a live, post-tag, operator-gated observation -- this dispatch has no DNS access for the dev.mcphost TXT record and no repository-secrets access for MCPHOST_REGISTRY_PRIVATE_KEY, both Joe's own open questions. The publish job is still fully wired in registry.yml (gated on the tag ref, needs: check) so it starts working the moment both exist, rather than being left unwritten.
additional.requirement_5_p2_is_out_of_this_dispatch: Requirement 5 (P2, "the entry's description includes the three starter tools' names") has no AC of its own and is not in this dispatch's assigned AC list (1/2/3/4/6); the PRD also never names which three tools, so implementing it would mean guessing. Left undone per the dispatch's own "do not start any work beyond this list" instruction -- see non_goals.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a committed, generated server.json matter instead of hand-writing one entry once and forgetting it?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own grounding and the pre-existing root server.json (a different, tenant-reconcile-owned artifact, PRD-mcphost-registry-publish) both show the failure mode directly: docs/launch/wave1-checklist.md records that file going stale at version 0.14.0 against the repo's real 0.64.0. A generator plus a --check CI gate makes that drift a build failure instead of a silent, discovered-months-later mismatch.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't this reuse the pre-existing host.registry_publish / src/registry.rs machinery instead of a new module?
five_whys_trace.a: That machinery publishes a TENANT's own domain-verified namespace entry at runtime, with no Cargo.toml involvement at all -- it answers "what is this tenant's tool server," not "what is mcphost itself." The PRD's own grounding states this directly: "host_registry_publish ... is unrelated."

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the committed artifact need its own pinned schema file instead of just trusting the generator's own shape?
five_whys_trace.a: The generator is this crate's own code, so a bug in it would pass its own output trivially; AC3's whole point is an independent check against the real upstream contract (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io's own schema) that the generator can't quietly drift from without a test noticing.

five_whys_trace.q: Why gate the live publish on a tag instead of publishing on every green push?
five_whys_trace.a: The registry's own version field is meant to track actual releases, not every commit; the PRD's own requirement 4 and AC5 both say "on tag v*", matching the existing release convention (CHANGELOG.md's own version-per-tag entries) rather than inventing a second cadence.

five_whys_trace.q: Why default $MCPHOST_PUBLIC_URL to https://mcphost.dev here specifically, instead of reusing `mcphost serve`'s own http://{bind} fallback?
five_whys_trace.a: This subcommand's whole job is describing the already-public listing for a reader who is not this process's own operator -- an unset env var here means "the production default", where `serve`'s own fallback exists only to give a freshly-bound socket with no public DNS yet SOME url to put in its own responses before the operator sets one.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does AC1's "name, description, version equal to Cargo.toml" mean `name` is literally Cargo.toml's bare package name?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- the upstream schema requires `name` to contain exactly one `/` (namespace/server-name), which "mcphost" alone fails. `name` is built from Cargo.toml's package name plus the dev.mcphost namespace Joe decided; see hard_constraints.name_is_not_literally_cargo_pkg_name.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should `license` be added even though it's not in the pinned upstream schema's own field list?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes -- the PRD's own requirement 2 asks for it, and neither Server nor ServerDetail sets additionalProperties:false, so it validates cleanly. See hard_constraints.license_field_is_not_in_the_upstream_schema.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is requirement 5 (P2, starter-tool names in the description) in scope for this dispatch?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- it has no AC of its own, is not in the dispatch's assigned AC list, and the PRD never names which three tools; implementing it would mean guessing. See hard_constraints.requirement_5_p2_is_out_of_this_dispatch_scope.
